previous_statement: Factorization and ledger. For n=1, node 1.1.1 makes mu_1:B->directsum S_{Pi_j,Pi_k} a linear bijection; the hypothesis that every gamma_jk is bijective makes Gamma_1 a linear bijection; and node 1.1.2 makes alpha_1:directsum S_{P_j,P_k}->A a linear bijection. Therefore gamma=alpha_1 Gamma_1 mu_1 is bijective. Because the datum fixes the same four level-one maps at all levels, the assembled gamma_n equals I_n tensor gamma. Let e_* be the minimum of e_blk, the preliminary-modulus and quadratic-bootstrap thresholds, and the fixed universal admissibility ceiling implicit in the epsilon-C* and compressed-corner definitions; reduce that standing epsilon ceiling to e_*/2 and set a_merge=e_*/2, so rho<=a_merge implies e=rho+epsilon<=e_*. Set C_merge=max{K_hom,K_norm,3}. Nodes 1.2 and 1.3 then say every amplification is a C_merge(rho+epsilon)-inclusion, and bijectivity of gamma makes it an extended C_merge(rho+epsilon)-isomorphism by def-extended-delta-inclusion.
new_statement: Corrected conditional ledger and obstruction. Let e_0>0 be the minimum of e_blk and every smallness threshold used in nodes 1.2 and 1.3. If one adds the hypothesis epsilon<=e_0/2, then choosing a_merge=e_0/2 gives e=rho+epsilon<=e_0 whenever rho<=a_merge. Subject to validation of nodes 1.1.1, 1.1.2, 1.2, and 1.3, the factorization gamma=alpha_1 Gamma_1 mu_1 is a composition of linear bijections, gamma_n=I_n tensor gamma, and with C_merge=max{K_hom,K_norm,3}, every amplification is a C_merge*e-inclusion; hence gamma is an extended C_merge*e-isomorphism by def-extended-delta-inclusion. However, the allowed root hypotheses contain no bound on epsilon, so no choice of a_merge controlling rho alone implies e<=e_0. Thus this argument proves only the corrected theorem with the additional hypothesis epsilon<=e_0/2 and does not prove the root contract as written.
